name: pricing-frequency-toggle

frames.best_why: The yearly view is settled: all three prices rolled, discount badges showing and the full grid aligned.
frames.render_note: The bottom edge of all three cards is clipped by the crop, so the action buttons are only half visible.

tagline: Three plan cards with a monthly-yearly switch that rolls the prices.
summary: A three-tier pricing block: a centred heading, a small sliding monthly or yearly switch, and three plan cards whose prices animate to the new figure while percentage-off badges pop in for yearly billing.
appearance: A centred heading and a line of grey subtext sit above a small two-option pill switch. Under them are three thin-bordered dark cards, the middle one slightly larger with a Popular badge, each holding a plan name, a big price, a billed label and a list of ticked features.
behaviour: Clicking monthly or yearly slides a small light highlight between the two labels. The prices roll digit by digit to the new amount, and in the yearly view a discount percentage fades in at the top-right of each card, then out again when you switch back.
demo_content: Basic, Pro and Business plans at $7, $17 and $49 a month with blog-post and transcription features.
search_phrases: three plan cards with a monthly yearly switch
price numbers roll when billing changes
saas pricing table with discount badges
plan comparison cards with feature ticks
toggle that animates the price per month
how to add a billing period switcher
use_when: A SaaS marketing page needs three tiers and a clear monthly versus yearly comparison.
avoid_when: Plan names, prices and features are hardcoded in the file, so real plans mean editing the source array.
customise: The three plans, their monthly and yearly prices, features and button labels live in the plans array. Currency is fixed to USD, so other markets need a source edit.
weight_why: Three static cards plus a sliding highlight and digit transitions only when billing changes.

a11y.note: The switch is labelled and exposes its pressed state, but the feature ticks are bare icons and the switch buttons use default focus styling.

issues: The bottom of the cards is clipped by the crop, so the call-to-action buttons are only half visible.
Prices are formatted as USD in the source, with no prop to change the currency.
polish_why: Tidy standard pricing grid with a smooth rolling price; conventional styling.
title: Pricing Frequency Toggle
